notes.definition: The theory of evolution by natural selection is now widely accepted because there is strong evidence for it: we know that characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes, the fossil record shows how organisms have changed over time, and we can see antibiotic resistance evolving in bacteria.
explanation: Evolution is a change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through a process of natural selection, which may result in the formation of a new species. When Darwin published his theory in 1859, many people did not accept it. One reason was that there was not enough evidence, and in particular nobody knew how characteristics were passed from parents to offspring. Today the theory of evolution by natural selection is widely accepted by scientists because a large amount of evidence has been gathered that supports it.

The first piece of evidence is that it has been shown that characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes. Darwin could see that offspring resembled their parents, but he could not explain how variation was inherited. We now know that genes are sections of DNA, that mutations produce new alleles, and that alleles are passed on in gametes. This explains how an advantageous characteristic can be passed to the next generation and become more common, exactly as natural selection predicts.

The second piece of evidence is the fossil record. Fossils are the remains of organisms from millions of years ago, found in rocks. Rock layers are usually laid down with the oldest at the bottom, so fossils in deeper layers are generally older. By comparing fossils from different layers, scientists can see how much or how little organisms have changed as life developed on Earth. The oldest rocks contain only simple organisms, and more complex organisms appear in younger rocks, which fits the idea of gradual change over a very long time.

The fossil record is incomplete. Many early forms of life were soft-bodied, so they left few traces, and many traces that did form have been destroyed by geological activity such as the movement and melting of rocks. This means there are gaps in the fossil record, and scientists cannot be certain how life began on Earth. However, the fossils that have been found still show a pattern of change over time that supports evolution.

The third piece of evidence is the way antibiotic resistance evolves in bacteria. Bacteria reproduce very quickly, sometimes dividing every 20 minutes, so many generations are produced in a short time. A random mutation may make one bacterium resistant to an antibiotic. When the antibiotic is used, non-resistant bacteria are killed but the resistant bacteria survive and reproduce, so the resistant strain becomes more common. This is natural selection happening fast enough for us to observe it directly.

Together these different types of evidence point to the same conclusion. When several independent lines of evidence support an explanation, scientists have more confidence in it. A scientific theory such as evolution is not a guess: it is an explanation that is supported by a large amount of evidence and has been tested many times.
keyFacts: The theory of evolution by natural selection is now widely accepted.
Evidence: characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes.
Evidence: the fossil record shows how organisms have changed over time.
Evidence: antibiotic resistance evolving in bacteria.
Fossils are the remains of organisms from millions of years ago, found in rocks.
Deeper rock layers are usually older, so fossils show the order in which organisms lived.
The fossil record is incomplete because early soft-bodied organisms left few traces and geological activity destroyed many.
Bacteria reproduce quickly, so natural selection can be seen happening within a few years.
Darwin could not explain how characteristics were inherited; the discovery of genes filled this gap.

keyTerms.definition: A change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through a process of natural selection, which may result in the formation of a new species.
The process in which individuals with characteristics best suited to the environment are more likely to survive, reproduce and pass on their alleles.
The remains of an organism from millions of years ago, found in rocks.
All the fossils that have been found, which together show how organisms have changed over time.
The ability of a strain of bacteria to survive treatment with an antibiotic, caused by a mutation.
A small section of DNA on a chromosome that codes for a protein; genes pass characteristics from parents to offspring.
An explanation of observations that is supported by a large amount of evidence and has been tested.

workedExamples.title: How fast can a bacterial population grow?
workedExamples.question: A single resistant bacterium divides once every 20 minutes. Assuming all the offspring survive, how many bacteria will there be after 2 hours?
steps: Convert the time to minutes: 2 hours = 120 minutes.
The population doubles at each division, so number = 2⁶.
workedExamples.answer: 64 bacteria. Rapid reproduction is why evolution in bacteria can be observed quickly.

workedExamples.title: Using fossils in rock layers as evidence
workedExamples.question: Rock layer A lies above rock layer B. Layer B contains fossils of simple shelled sea animals only. Layer A contains the same type of shelled animals plus fossils of early fish. Explain how this supports the theory of evolution.
steps: Rock layers are usually laid down with the oldest at the bottom, so layer B is older than layer A.
The older layer contains only simpler organisms.
Fish appear later in the younger layer, showing new types of organism have developed over time.
This pattern of change over time is what evolution predicts.
workedExamples.answer: The older (lower) layer contains simpler organisms and new organisms appear in younger layers, showing that life has changed over time.

workedExamples.title: Calculating a percentage increase in resistant infections
workedExamples.question: In a hospital, the number of infections caused by a resistant strain of bacteria rose from 120 in one year to 300 five years later. Calculate the percentage increase.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think 'theory' means evolution is just a guess.
misconceptions.right: In fact, a scientific theory is an explanation supported by a large amount of evidence. Evolution by natural selection is supported by genes, fossils and antibiotic resistance.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the antibiotic causes the mutation that makes bacteria resistant.
misconceptions.right: In fact, the mutation happens at random. The antibiotic only selects: it kills non-resistant bacteria so the resistant ones survive and reproduce.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the fossil record is complete, so it shows every step of evolution.
misconceptions.right: In fact, there are gaps because soft-bodied organisms rarely fossilise and geological activity destroys many fossils.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think Darwin knew about genes.
misconceptions.right: In fact, Darwin did not know how characteristics were inherited. The discovery that characteristics are passed on in genes came later and strongly supports his theory.

realWorld: Doctors track the spread of antibiotic-resistant bacteria such as MRSA, which is evolution by natural selection happening in hospitals today.
Museums and geologists use fossils in rock layers to work out the order in which groups of organisms appeared on Earth.
Understanding how resistance evolves guides advice on using antibiotics only when needed and finishing the course.
examTips: When asked for evidence for evolution, name fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria; you can add that characteristics are passed on in genes.
For antibiotic resistance, always say the mutation is random and that the antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria, leaving resistant ones to survive and reproduce.
Explain why bacteria are good evidence: they reproduce quickly, so you can see many generations and the change happening.
If asked why the fossil record is incomplete, give two reasons: soft-bodied organisms left few traces, and geological activity destroyed traces.
For bacterial growth calculations, find the number of divisions first, then use 2 to the power of that number.
summary: Evolution by natural selection is now widely accepted.
Evidence 1: characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes.
Evidence 2: the fossil record shows organisms changing over time.
Evidence 3: antibiotic resistance evolving in bacteria can be observed directly.
The fossil record has gaps, so we cannot be certain how life began.
Several independent lines of evidence make scientists more confident in the theory.

questions.question: Which of these provides evidence for the theory of evolution?
options: The fossil record
The water cycle
Photosynthesis in leaves
Vaccination against measles
markScheme: 1 mark: the fossil record
questions.explanation: Fossils show how organisms have changed over millions of years. The other options are real processes but do not show inherited change over time.

questions.question: How do most scientists view the theory of evolution by natural selection today?
options: It has been rejected by most scientists
It is only a guess with no evidence
It is widely accepted
It has been shown to be false by DNA evidence
markScheme: 1 mark: it is widely accepted
questions.explanation: The theory is widely accepted because of strong evidence. DNA and genes support it rather than disprove it.

questions.question: What are characteristics passed on to offspring in?
options: Blood
Genes
Cytoplasm
Cell walls
markScheme: 1 mark: genes
questions.explanation: Characteristics are inherited in genes, which are sections of DNA. The old idea that characteristics are carried in blood is wrong.

questions.question: Why can evolution be observed in bacteria within a few years?
options: Bacteria are very small
Bacteria have no DNA
Bacteria never mutate
Bacteria reproduce at a fast rate
markScheme: 1 mark: bacteria reproduce at a fast rate
questions.explanation: Fast reproduction means many generations in a short time, so changes spread quickly. Bacteria do have DNA and do mutate; their size is not the reason.

questions.question: How do fossils provide evidence for evolution?
options: They show that organisms have never changed
They show how much or how little organisms have changed over time
They show which genes an organism had
They show that all organisms lived at the same time
markScheme: 1 mark: they show how much or how little organisms have changed over time
questions.explanation: Comparing fossils from rocks of different ages shows how organisms have changed. Fossils do not normally contain usable genes, and they show organisms lived at different times.

questions.question: A population of bacteria contains one bacterium with a mutation that makes it resistant to an antibiotic. The antibiotic is then used. What happens?
options: All the bacteria become resistant because of the antibiotic
All the bacteria are killed
Non-resistant bacteria are killed; the resistant bacterium survives and reproduces
The resistant bacterium is killed first because it is different
markScheme: 1 mark: non-resistant bacteria are killed; the resistant one survives and reproduces
questions.explanation: This is natural selection: the antibiotic removes non-resistant bacteria, leaving the resistant one to multiply. The antibiotic does not cause resistance, and the resistant one is not killed.

questions.question: Which piece of knowledge, unknown in Darwin's time, now strongly supports his theory?
options: That characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes
That the Earth is round
That animals need food to survive
That some animals are bigger than others
markScheme: 1 mark: characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes
questions.explanation: Darwin could not explain how variation was inherited. The discovery of genes provided the mechanism. The other options were already known in Darwin's time.

questions.question: Why is antibiotic resistance in bacteria particularly useful evidence for evolution?
options: It proves that all bacteria are harmful
It shows that antibiotics cause mutations
It explains how life first began on Earth
It lets scientists observe natural selection happening in a short time
markScheme: 1 mark: natural selection can be observed in a short time
questions.explanation: Fossils show change over millions of years, but resistant bacteria evolve within years, so scientists can watch it happen. Antibiotics do not cause mutations, and resistance tells us nothing about how life began.

questions.question: Which observation, if it were found, would NOT fit the theory of evolution?
options: Simple organisms found in older rock layers than more complex organisms
Fossils of modern mammals found in the oldest rock layers, below the earliest fish fossils
Bacteria becoming resistant after an antibiotic has been used for several years
Offspring inheriting alleles from their parents
markScheme: 1 mark: fossils of modern mammals in the oldest rock layers, below the earliest fish
questions.explanation: Evolution predicts that complex organisms such as mammals appeared long after simpler ones, so they should not be found in the oldest layers. The other three observations are all expected if evolution has happened.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why the fossil record is incomplete?
options: Fossils only form from animals, never from plants
Scientists have stopped looking for new fossils
Many early organisms were soft-bodied and left few traces, and many traces were destroyed by geological activity
Fossils only formed during the last few thousand years
markScheme: 1 mark: soft-bodied organisms left few traces and geological activity destroyed many
questions.explanation: Both reasons in the correct answer are from the specification. Plant fossils do exist, scientists still search for fossils, and fossils formed over millions of years.

questions.question: A bacterium divides once every 20 minutes. Starting with one bacterium, and assuming all offspring survive, calculate the number of bacteria after 2 hours.
markScheme: 1 mark: number of divisions = 120 ÷ 20 = 6
1 mark: 2⁶ = 64
questions.explanation: 2 hours is 120 minutes, so there are 6 divisions. The number doubles each time: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64.

questions.question: A single antibiotic-resistant bacterium survives treatment. It divides once every 20 minutes. Assuming all offspring survive, calculate how many resistant bacteria there will be after 5 hours.
markScheme: 1 mark: number of divisions = 300 ÷ 20 = 15
1 mark: 2¹⁵ = 32 768
questions.explanation: 5 hours = 300 minutes. 300 ÷ 20 = 15 divisions, so the number is 2¹⁵ = 32 768. This shows how quickly a resistant strain can become common.

questions.question: An antibiotic kills 99.9% of a population of 2 000 000 bacteria. The survivors are all resistant. Calculate how many bacteria survive.
markScheme: 1 mark: percentage surviving = 100 − 99.9 = 0.1%
questions.explanation: Only 0.1% survive: 2 000 000 × 0.001 = 2000. Even a tiny surviving fraction is a large number of bacteria that can reproduce to form a resistant population.

questions.question: The number of infections caused by a resistant strain of bacteria in a hospital rose from 120 in 2015 to 300 in 2020. Calculate the percentage increase.
markScheme: 1 mark: increase = 300 − 120 = 180
questions.explanation: Percentage increase = increase ÷ original value × 100. A common mistake is to divide by the new value (180 ÷ 300 = 60%), which is wrong.

questions.question: Give two types of evidence for evolution.
markScheme: 1 mark each, any two: fossils / the fossil record; antibiotic resistance in bacteria; characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes
questions.explanation: The specification names fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria, and the discovery that characteristics are inherited in genes.

questions.question: What is a fossil?
acceptedAnswers: remains of organisms from millions of years ago
markScheme: 1 mark: the remains of an organism from millions of years ago, found in rocks
questions.explanation: A fossil is the preserved remains or traces of an organism from millions of years ago, found in rocks.

questions.question: Name a strain of bacteria that is resistant to antibiotics.
markScheme: 1 mark: MRSA
questions.explanation: MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) is the example named in the specification.

questions.question: Define evolution.
markScheme: 1 mark: a change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time
1 mark: through natural selection, which may result in the formation of a new species
questions.explanation: Note it is populations that evolve, not individuals, and the change must be in inherited characteristics.

questions.question: Explain why the discovery that characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes supports Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection.
markScheme: 1 mark: Darwin could not explain how characteristics / variation were inherited
1 mark: genes provide the mechanism: advantageous alleles are passed on to offspring so become more common
questions.explanation: Natural selection only works if advantageous characteristics are inherited. Genes explain how this happens.

questions.question: Describe how fossils found in different rock layers show that organisms have changed over time.
markScheme: 1 mark: deeper / lower rock layers are usually older
1 mark: fossils in older layers are different (often simpler) from those in younger layers, showing gradual change
questions.explanation: Rock layers form a timeline. Comparing fossils from layer to layer shows how much or how little organisms have changed.

questions.question: Darwin's theory was not widely accepted when it was published in 1859, but it is widely accepted today. Suggest why.
markScheme: 1 mark: much more evidence is now available
1 mark: e.g. genes explain inheritance / more fossils found / antibiotic resistance observed in bacteria
questions.explanation: Scientific theories become accepted as evidence builds up. In 1859 there was no explanation of inheritance and fewer fossils.

questions.question: Explain how the development of antibiotic resistance in bacteria provides evidence for evolution by natural selection.
markScheme: 1 mark: a random mutation makes some bacteria resistant
1 mark: the antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria, so resistant bacteria survive and reproduce
1 mark: the resistant strain becomes more common: a change in inherited characteristics of the population, which is evolution
questions.explanation: Each step of natural selection is visible: variation from mutation, a selection pressure (the antibiotic), survival and reproduction of the best suited, and a change in the population.

questions.question: Suggest why scientists can observe the evolution of antibiotic resistance in bacteria within a few years, but cannot observe the evolution of elephants in a human lifetime.
markScheme: 1 mark: bacteria reproduce very quickly so many generations are produced in a short time
1 mark: elephants take many years to reproduce, so only a few generations occur in a human lifetime
questions.explanation: Natural selection acts each generation. The number of generations, not the number of years, controls how fast a population can change.

questions.question: Explain why scientists cannot be certain how life began on Earth.
markScheme: 1 mark: many early forms of life were soft-bodied so left few traces / fossils
1 mark: traces that did form have mainly been destroyed by geological activity
questions.explanation: Without fossils from the earliest life, there is very little direct evidence of how life started.

questions.question: A student says: 'Evolution is only a theory, so there is no real evidence for it.' Evaluate this statement.
markScheme: 1 mark: the statement is wrong: a scientific theory is an explanation supported by a lot of evidence
1 mark: e.g. fossils show organisms changing over time
1 mark: e.g. antibiotic resistance can be observed evolving / characteristics are passed on in genes, so the theory is widely accepted
questions.explanation: In everyday speech 'theory' can mean a guess, but in science it means a well-tested explanation. Back up the evaluation with specific evidence.

questions.question: Describe the evidence that supports the theory of evolution by natural selection.
markScheme: Indicative content: characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes, explaining how advantageous characteristics are inherited; fossils are remains of organisms from millions of years ago found in rocks; fossils in different rock layers show how organisms have changed over time; simpler organisms in older rocks; antibiotic resistance in bacteria: random mutation, resistant bacteria survive antibiotic and reproduce, resistant strain becomes more common; bacteria reproduce quickly so evolution can be observed; MRSA as an example.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): at least two types of evidence described clearly, with an explanation of how each supports the theory.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): types of evidence named with little description.
questions.explanation: Name each type of evidence and say how it supports the theory. Just listing 'fossils, bacteria' only reaches Level 1.

questions.question: When Darwin published his theory of evolution by natural selection in 1859, many scientists did not accept it. Explain why the theory is widely accepted by scientists today. Refer to at least two types of evidence in your answer.
markScheme: Indicative content: in 1859 there was insufficient evidence; the mechanism of inheritance was not known; since then it has been shown that characteristics are passed on to offspring in genes (DNA); mutations produce new alleles giving variation; advantageous alleles are passed on, explaining natural selection; more fossils have been found; fossils in rock layers show how organisms changed gradually over millions of years; older layers contain simpler organisms; the fossil record has gaps (soft-bodied organisms, geological activity) but the pattern still supports evolution; antibiotic resistance in bacteria: random mutation gives resistance, antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria, resistant ones survive and reproduce, resistant strains such as MRSA become common; bacteria reproduce quickly so evolution can be observed directly; several independent lines of evidence all support the same theory.

Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): a detailed, coherent explanation of at least two types of evidence, each clearly linked to how it supports natural selection, with reference to why acceptance has increased since 1859.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): two types of evidence described with some explanation, or one explained in detail.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements naming evidence with little explanation.
questions.explanation: Strong answers contrast 1859 (little evidence, no knowledge of genes) with today, then explain in detail how genes, fossils and resistant bacteria each support natural selection.

questions.question:
A hospital recorded the percentage of infections caused by one species of bacterium that were resistant to a particular antibiotic.
2000: 5%
2004: 18%
2008: 32%
2012: 41%
The antibiotic was used widely throughout this period. Describe the trend and explain how it provides evidence for evolution.
markScheme: Indicative content: the percentage of resistant infections increased every year recorded, from 5% to 41%; the rate of increase slowed slightly in later years (13, 14 then 9 percentage points); resistance originally arose by random mutation; wide use of the antibiotic killed non-resistant bacteria; resistant bacteria survived and reproduced, passing on the allele for resistance; so the proportion of resistant bacteria in the population increased; this is a change in inherited characteristics of a population over time by natural selection, which is evolution.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): the trend is described using data and clearly explained by natural selection, linked to evolution.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): the trend is described simply, or natural selection is mentioned without linking to the data.
questions.explanation: Quote data when describing a trend (from 5% in 2000 to 41% in 2012). Then explain the rise using mutation, selection by the antibiotic, survival, reproduction and inheritance.
